observations.observation: As per policy all employee files should be available in the branch. During current audit visit, it was observed that few files of transfer-in employees were still not provided to branch. Detail is mentioned in the below appended table;

observations.title: Disposal Note not Prepared for Obsolete/Broken Items
observations.observation: For effective use of company resources, branch should either get the assets repaired or report them to CSO for disposal through AIDN. During the audit, a number of assets were found in the branch, which were not in working condition and for which disposal note was not prepared by the branch. For detail please refer to Annexure-A.
observations.recommendation: For effective use of company resources, surplus assets should be timely intimated through AIDN to the competent authority so that these assets can be utilized where they needed. As per SOM, clause # E-1.5 (a); “Where a Branch/SGO/RO has surplus assets for any reason, the same shall be communicated to the Manager P&AM at the RO on the Assets Inspection and Disposal Note (AIDN), through proper channels.”

observations.title: Discrepancies in Printed Stationery Register
observations.observation: Printed stationery register should be properly maintained. Certain discrepancies were found in Printed Stationery Register. Such as; Printed Stationery record Before 2019 not available The branch had started maintaining printed stationery register in 2019. There was no previous record. Register not Validated by Branch Head Printed Stationery Register should be validated with the intervals as prescribed by the SOM. However, the register was not being validated as prescribed in SOM.
observations.recommendation: As per SOM, Clause, E-2.4; “Following Stock Registers shall also be maintained by the Branch. Printed Stationery Register” Printed Stationery Register Designated Official by BH Quarterly The branch management is requested to retrieve the list of printed stationery received from CSO and check completion of the register. The register should be checked/validated on required intervals. As per SOM, Clause, E-2.3 PRINTED STATIONERY REGISTER, d); “The Printed Stationery Register shall be checked and signed by the BH on a quarterly basis”.

observations.title: Photocopy Contract Awarded on Higher rate
observations.observation: Purchases/Services should be made with due diligence. During verification of the branch’s routine procurement transactions (on sample basis), it was observed that photocopies contract had been awarded on higher rate. Detail of some instances is as under;

observations.title: Purchase Committee not Functioning as Defined in SOM
observations.observation: Purchase committee is not actively involved in procurement related activities, as defined in school operations manual. During discussions with PC members it was concluded that the committee members are involved only in purchase of Stationery and entertainment. There was no involvement of two PC members in Repair & Maintenance related jobs like formal prequalification of vendors, advisory services, surety of equal opportunity buyer, review of comparative statement, negotiations, monitoring of vendor’s services etc.
observations.recommendation: Members should actively be involved in the function of Purchase Committee, as per School Operations Manual Clause G-1-4e & H-1-6b: “General functions of PC would be as follows: Review sourcing / pre-qualification of potential vendors. Recommend suspension, removal or reinstatement of vendors. Review and provide advice to Branch Head, on whether proposed Procurement actions are in accordance with the Company Procurement policies. Ensure that equal opportunity is provided to every genuine competitor. Review and evaluate bids, tenders, comparative statements and related documents submitted. Review negotiated price, terms & conditions, where situation warrants. Review suggestions / complaints by the end users.” “For day to day repair and maintenance activities, a designated person of the Branch, in coordination with the Branch Purchase Committee (PC), shall search for suitable contractors/vendors”.

observations.title: Ledger Accounts not Matching with CSON Books
observations.observation: In branch books an amount of PKR. 8,090/- was appearing as receivable from CSO against re-imbursements. Contrary to this, as per CSO books of account, an amount of PKR. 64,600/- is also receivable from the Branch on dated 15-Jan-2020. This was creating an embarrassing situation where amounts are receivable in the books of accounts of both the parties. Moreover, the Branch Accountant was unable to conclude by preparing reconciliation with CSO records.
observations.recommendation: Branch needs to coordinate Cluster Support Office to resolve the issue. Referred to CSO Referred to Branch Head

observations.title: Delay Reimbursement Received from CSO
observations.observation: Branch is allocated limited budget against each head of account. Late reimbursements from CSO may lead to shortage of funds in the branch. During audit it was observed that reimbursements claims dispatched by branch on time while CSO was reimbursed to branch with delay. For detail please refer to Annexure-B.
observations.recommendation: Reimbursements should be processed on time. This may lead to shortage of funds for the branch. As per SOM clause, D-3.4, “All reimbursement claims received shall be checked by respective Accounts department within 20 days of their receipt”. Referred to CSO

observations.title: Vendors Registration not Performed by Branch
observations.observation: Vendor Registration Application (VRA) form should be filled by the vendors of the branch, however, in audited branch it was observed that (VRA) Vendors Registration of major supplier were not performed by the branch.
observations.recommendation: Vendor registration should be performed by the branch as vendor registration is an important process for all vendors wishing to supply material or services to the company. Vendor registration helps in updation of vendor details and monitoring of vendor performance. As per procurement manual Clause 6.2.3 “Vendor shall submit the completed vendor registration application along with required documents (if any) to respective procurement department or accounts office (in-case of branches) which shall be forwarded promptly to the branch PC". As per procurement manual Clause 6.8.6; “The files of applicants / vendors shall also be maintained by the designated officer of P&AM department / PC (in-case of branches) and be available for review by Head of P&AM and authorized P&AM staff.”

observations.title: Discrepancies noted in Vouchers Processing
observations.observation: As per standard accounting practice, all vouchers are to be signed by Accountant on “Prepared By” & Branch Head on “Approved By”. Further, acknowledgment should also be obtained from the person to whom the payment were During the audit it was observed that in some cases the vouchers were not signed by the branch official. Some instances are as under:

observations.title: List of Common Suppliers not Available in the Branch
observations.observation: List of common vendors should be available in the branch for the deduction of Income tax. It was observed during the audit that lists of preferred vendors was not available in the branch.
observations.recommendation: List of common vendors should be timely provided by CSO for the deduction of withholding tax. Referred to CSO

observations.title: Branch Address Used by the Photocopier
observations.observation: The vendor who provide any service (s) to the BSS branches were required to use their own business address (es). However, during audit it was observed that the vendor (s) who provide the photocopier services to the branch were using the BSS branch address in their bills.
observations.recommendation: The vendors should use their own business address in bills/invoices.

observations.title: Negative Balance of Cash in Hand Account
observations.observation: As per company policy, the balance of Cash in hand should not be negative. But while checking the cash ledger it was observed that closing balance of cash account was negative on many occasions. Instances have been mentioned in below table: Balance (Credit)
observations.recommendation: The balance of cash in hand account should not be negative. Proper care should be exercised while recording transactions in Imprest Module. Further Personal Cash should not be mixed with the official cash in hand.

observations.title: Cheque Number not Fed in Module
observations.observation: Cheque number must be fed in imprest module. During audit it was observed that cheque number of few payments were not fed in imprest module. For detail please refer to Annexure-D.
observations.recommendation: Cheque number must be fed in imprest module. This will be helpful in the preparing the Bank Reconciliation Statement.

observations.title: Delay in Confirmation of Employees
observations.observation: Employees should be confirmed after completion of probationary period and their confirmation letters should be issued without any delay. During audit, we found that there was some delay in this regard. Few of the instances are mentioned below: Faheem Akhtar 10/Aug/15 01-Aug-16 Rushda Tasleem 25/Aug/15 01-Aug-16 Shafaq Farooq 1/Oct/15 01-Dec-16 Muhammad Umair 1/Oct/15 01-Jul-16 Samra Imran 8/Aug/16 01-May-17 Sadia Tareen 8/Aug/16 01-May-17 Naila Javed 2/Jan/17 01-Oct-17 Irfan Aslam 12/Jan/17 01-Oct-17 Aiza Zahoor 15/Feb/18 01-Nov-18 Samia Batool Tahir 5/Nov/18 01-Nov-19 Noureen Anjum 7/Nov/18 01-Nov-19 Saleem Maseeh 8/Nov/18 01-Aug-19 Khalid Hussain 16/Jul/19 01-May-20 Syeda Zainab Gardezi 1/Aug/19 01-Jun-20 Abdul Rauf 26/Aug/19 01-Jul-20 Asghar Khalid 2/Sep/19 01-Aug-20 Sidra Aslam 25/Sep/19 01-Jun-20 Arooj Fatima 27/Sep/19 01-Jun-20 Warisha Babar 1/Nov/19 01-Jul-20 Umer Zeeshan 31/Oct/19 01-Sep-20
observations.recommendation: Probation period should not be un-necessarily prolonged and the office order for the confirmation of services should be issued on timely basis. In case of unsatisfactory performance, the Line Manager may extend the probation period for an additional three (03) months.”
observations.audit_view: Azhar Qayoom confirmation was delayed for more than 1 month as per the BEAMS record. Further above mentioned teachers were hired before January so they should have been confirmed after compeletion of their probationery period of 6 months.

observations.title: Livery Items providing with Delay
observations.observation: Livery items should be provided to junior staff on timely basis as directed in livery manual. During audit, it was observed that branch provided livery items with significant delay to support staff. Detail is as under;

observations.title: Incomplete Bar Code Labelling on Library Books
observations.observation: Bar Codes facilitate issuance of books through library module (KOHA). All books should have bar codes pasted on them. During audit, it was informed by the branch librarian(s) that the barcode labelling was not done on approximately 300 Library books in Early Year and Middle/Senior wings of the Library. RecommendationBar Codes should be pasted on all books on timely basis. As per Library ManualChapter # 15 “Arrangement of Books on the Shelf”; “After allocating the class number, cataloguing and labelling etc., books should be arranged on the shelf.”
observations.recommendation: Books should be issued through the library module. As per e-mail from Director of Studies dated 21.12.2010; “All librarians must work both on the ‘Library Module’ and ‘Manually’. Accession registers have not been withdrawn yet.” The entry of Library Books in module should be completed at the earliest.
observations.audit_view: Due to the time constraint this rectification could not be verified. CSO-C Librarian is requested to please ensure that all the books are now accessed.

observations.title: Difference in Quantity of Books Transfer from BEAMS to KOHA Module
observations.observation: During audit it was observed that the number of books transferred from BEAMS to KOHA Accession Register was 5601 while the books appearing in KOHA were 5551 with a difference of 50 books.
observations.recommendation: All books fed in BEAMS module should be transferred to KOHA module. Referred to CSO

observations.title: Books not Issued through KOHA Module
observations.observation: Library books should be issued through library module KOHA and through manual issuance system as well. It was noted during the audit that issuance of library books through Library module was not in practice since May-19. Manual register was used to issue the books to the teachers and book cards were used for the issuance of books to the students.
observations.recommendation: Books should be issued through KOHA module. As per e-mail from Director of Studies dated 21 Dec 2010; “All librarians must work both on the ‘Library Module’ and ‘Manually’. Accession registers have not been withdrawn yet.” Referred to CSO Referred to Branch Head

observations.title: UPS Facility not Available with Library Computer
observations.observation: As per library manual UPS should be attached with librarian computer. However, there was no UPS available with librarian computer, due to which, the librarian has no backup facility in case of power failure during current load shedding.
observations.recommendation: For smooth running of BEAMS module, UPS facility should be attached to the system and internet facility should be provided. As per Library manual the below clause is mentioned for reference. “UPS should be provided for BEAMS support.” Referred to CSO

observations.title: Slow Internet Speed in Library
observations.observation: KOHA system will be connected to an internet system to ensure its smooth function. However during audit it was found that the branch facing slow internet speed and due to which KOHA system did not work. Further, this will also result in difficulties in using of library module.
observations.recommendation: For smooth running / function of the KOHA system, a high speed internet facility should be provided.

observations.title: Employees ID Cards not in Practice
observations.observation: All school staff should have employee cards for security and recognition purposes. During current audit it was observed that BSS employee card of four employees were not made. Detail is mentioned in the below appended table; Employee ID # Zareen Wasim Haye 1-Aug-19 Ishaq Masih 15-Sep-18 Tayyaba Babar 15-Oct-18 Hira Tanveer 8-Jul-19
observations.recommendation: Employee cards should be immediately made after hiring of the employee.

observations.title: Unexploited Security Cameras Found in Branch
observations.observation: Security cameras should be installed and kept up-to-date for better performance and security of the branch. However, during audit it was observed that the branch had purchased four CCTV cameras on 27-Sep-19 but still not yet installed resulting in delay of 136 days. Recommendation The branch management should demand only those assets that are needed. Further, the assets (CCVT cameras) when purchased should be installed immediately to avoid any inevitable situation. Referred to CSO Auditee Response We demanded new DVR in CAPEX 2020-21 we will fix the problem as soon as we received the DVR. CSO Response In CAPEX 19/20, 4X new cameras were demanded for campus but received cameras are of high resolution ( 4 mega pixel) and they are not compatible with the present DVR and it is not supporting the newly issued cameras(no display). Case has been taken up with Supply & chain dept. for change of these cameras as per requisite specifications.

observations.title: Backup of Branch Data not Kept
observations.observation: Back up of the branch data like MS Excel files, MS Word files and MS PowerPoint files etc. of branch should be kept on some separate storage device to avoid any loss of date in case of any disorder. During audit it was observed that device was installed in branch but back up of branch’s data was never kept due to non-availability of device password.
observations.recommendation: The concerned administrative staff and IT teacher of branch are advised to develop an appropriate mechanism to take and secure backup of all important data in consultation with IT staff. As per IT policy para 1.4.4: “Ensure that record is backed up appropriately”.

observations.title: Validated Paintable Area Measurements not Available
observations.observation: As paint work is a regular annual exercise in the branch, record of total paintable area should be available in branch to avoid any ambiguity at the time of awarding paint work contracts. It was observed that the said document was not available at the branch.
observations.recommendation: In order keep track of annual paint work expense, branch should have an updated record of total paint area measurement duly endorsed by works department.

observations.title: Delay in Deposit of Withholding Tax
observations.observation: As per company policy, Withholding Tax should be deposited within seven days from the date of deduction. However, some delays were observed in the deposit of withholding tax deducted on the payments to suppliers/vendors. Detail of instances is given below: Tax Amount (PKR) (Excl 7 days) Basket pole Split A.C Termite Proofing Water filter Photocopy Postage Coaster Coaster Camera Repair Photography Lockers IT lab Photocopy Toner Tea Items
observations.recommendation: Tax policies should be strictly followed; any lapses in this regard may result in penalties to the company. As per DF letter number 10597 dated January 27, 2011: “Please follow the instructions at your end and also instruct the schools and other concerned staff to deduct the tax accordingly and Deposit the tax into Government Treasury within seven days from the deduction and payment”. Branch should maintain the record of Purchase/Service Requisition, According to policy: “There should be following copies of PR. 1st copy - Retained by the Branch. 2nd Copy - for Invoice”.

observations.title: Bills not Signed by PC Members
observations.observation: PC members are required to ensure the quantitative and qualitative aspects of procurements. Involvement of PC members also ensures selection of suitable vendors for procurements made by school. observations.recommendation: List of common suppliers should be timely provided by CSO for the deduction of withholding tax.

observations.title: Delayed Finalization of Final Settlement Cases
observations.observation: As per Policy, all final settlement cases should be processed within 45 days from the last working day of an employee. It was noted, that certain final settlement claims of employees were being finalized with significant delays. Detail of instances is mentioned in Annexure-E.
observations.recommendation: Final settlement claims should be processed on timely basis. All concerned authorities should play their role in finalizing the final settlement claims within the stipulated time. According to clause D-2.8.1(a) of School Operations Manual, “The final settlement of employees shall be paid within 45 days of their last working day”.

observations.title: Short Office Hours Observed for Staff
observations.observation: Branch Head should ensure that complete office hours are being followed by the employees. During sample based review of employee attendance, it was revealed that some of the branch staff was not following the official timings. The matter may affect operational efficiency of the Branch and also the leave encashment and salary of respective staff. Some of the instances are attached as Annexure-E.
observations.recommendation: Branch Head should monitor the working hours being served by the subordinate staff and in case of nonconformity; necessary steps such as short leave applications etc. should be taken for its adaptation. As per SOM, C-3. WORKING HOURS, b); Position Principals and HMs, SMs 30 minutes Before School Starts 90 minutes After School Ends Teachers on duty 30 minutes Before School Starts 30 minutes After School Ends Coordinators  and other teaching staff 15 minutes Before School Starts 15 minutes After School Ends Other Administrative and Office Staff 8 working hours (Work times determined by RH) Technical and Support Staff (other than guards) 8 working hours (Work times determined by RH) Guards 12 Working hours (Office timings to be determined by the respective RH or Head of Security , as the case may be) Security Supervisor 9 working hours (Office timings to be determined by the respective RH or Head of Security, as the case may be)

observations.title: Out Attendance not Marked
observations.observation: All staff members should mark the attendance while leaving the premises at off time. In case if the attendance is not marked, appropriate application should be furnished for the same. It was observed during the audit that at a number of times, neither the out attendance of certain employees was marked nor the application for the same was raised. A summary of such instances is mentioned in Annexure-Q.
observations.recommendation: Branch Head should monitor attendance being marked by the subordinate staff and in case of nonconformity; necessary steps should be taken for its adaptation. As per School Operations.Manual, clause 12.2.1; “Employees are expected to report to work as scheduled and on time. Employees shall mark their attendance on biometric devices (online attendance) installed in offices”.

observations.title: Delay in Deposit of Registration Fee
observations.observation: As per Company policy, Registration fee collected should be deposited on weekly basis or immediately where the amount of Registration fee collection reaches Rs.5,000 or more. Delays were observed while checking registration fee record and bank deposit slips. Instances are attached as Annexure-H.
observations.recommendation: Branch Head should ensure that all the receipts are deposited on timely basis. As per prescribed procedure mentioned in clause 1.3.11 of School Operations Manual; “Registration fee collected will be deposited on a weekly basis. However, where the amount collected through registration is Rs. 5,000 or more then the same shall be deposited irrespective of the completion of the week”.

observations.title: File of Transferred-In Student not Available
observations.observation: All Students’ files should be available in the branch. It was observed during audit visit that certain file of transferred in student were not available in the branch. Details are as follows: Sr. #

observations.title: Un-Matched Assets Found in Branch
observations.observation: Un-matched Assets i.e. the fixed assets that were present in the branch but not appearing in fixed assets register of branch. We observed some unmatched assets during sample verification of assets.Detail of few instances is as under:
observations.recommendation: The source from which these assets were received should be identified and fixed assets’ register should be updated after consulting the matter with RO.
observations.audit_view: Pending discrepancies should be rectified/resolved by the campus, with the consultation of ROC.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Laboratory Registers
observations.observation: In order to ensure smooth running of school science laboratories, laboratory stock registers and monthly consumable registers are maintained by laboratory in-charges and checked regularly by BH. Following irregularities were observed: Stock registers were not checked by BH. Calculation error found. Physical stock not matching with records. Stock received but not entered in register.
observations.recommendation: Laboratory Stock Registers should be checked by BH on monthly basis. As per Policy: “Branch Head shall verify the laboratory registers on monthly basis.” Items issued and received should be recorded on the stock registers. Physical balance shoud be matched with the records.

observations.title: Demolition Register not prepared
observations.observation: As per policy, a demolition register shall be maintained for scrap obtained as a result of demolition. It was observed that demolition register was not maintained at branch.
observations.recommendation: Demolition register should be maintained by branch for scrap. As per SOM, Clause H.1.9, e); “A demolition register shall be maintained at the Branch by the Caretaker or designated person, and should be vetted by the BH and RMO(Cluster). Its utilisation/disposal shall be recorded in the same register.”

observations.title: Purchase/Service Requisition Files not Maintained
observations.observation: A separate Purchase/service requisition file should be maintained in the branch. During audit it was noted that Files of purchase/service requisition were not being maintained.
observations.recommendation: Separate files should be used for filing of purchase/service requisitions & should be filed sequentially. As per SOM, clause 29.8.2: “Purchase requisitions shall be pre-numbered. There should be following copies of PR. 1st copyRetained by the Branch”

observations.title: Reimbursements Made with Delay by CSO
observations.observation: Branch is being allocated limited budget against each head of account, late reimbursements from CSO may lead to shortage of funds in the branch. During audit some instances were observed where reimbursements were finalized/disbursed with significant delay by CSO. Detail is attached as Annexure-I.
observations.recommendation: To avoid unnecessary delays and shortage of funds in branch, reimbursement claims should be processes on timely basis by CSO. As per Clause D-3.4(b) of School Operation Manual, “All reimbursement claims received shall be checked by the respective Accounts department within 20 days of their receipt”. Capex expenditure should not be incurred from imprest budget. In case of urgency such expenses may be incurred with the approval of CSO. Subsequently, reimbursement of such expenses should be claimed from CSO as the case may be. Concerned staff of CSO staff are requested to ensure that capex items are not being purchased from Imprest budget. Members should actively be involved in the function of Purchase Committee, as per School Operations Manual Clause G-1-4e & H-1-6b: “General functions of PC would be as follows: Review sourcing / pre-qualification of potential vendors. Recommend suspension, removal or reinstatement of vendors. Review and provide advice to Branch Head, on whether proposed Procurement actions are in accordance with the Company Procurement policies. Ensure that equal opportunity is provided to every genuine competitor. Review and evaluate bids, tenders, comparative statements and related documents submitted. Review negotiated price, terms & conditions, where situation warrants. Review suggestions / complaints by the end users.” “For day to day repair and maintenance activities, a designated person of the Branch, in coordination with the Branch Purchase Committee (PC), shall search for suitable contractors/vendors”.

observations.title: Approved Vendors List not Available with Branch
observations.observation: Branch should have approved list of preferred vendors for its daily and/or routine procurement. It was observed that such list was not prepared by purchase committee.
observations.recommendation: List of approved vendor should be available with the branch. As per School Operations Manual Clause G-1.6(d); “For day to day procurement activities, vendors may not be formally registered, but a list shall be maintained for preferred vendors. Officer responsible for procurement shall prepare list of suitable vendors/contractors. This list shall be reviewed/updated by the members of Purchase Committee”.

observations.title: Approved Copy of Handing/Taking Over of Branch Accountant not Available
observations.observation: Handing/taking over of branch accountant should be conducted by CSO at the time of change. During audit it was observed that approved copy of handing/taking over record not available in the branch. Mr. Muhammad Jamil (Ex. Accountant) handed over the responsibilities to Mr. Ali Yousaf (Current Accountant) on 25th April, 2019.
observations.recommendation: Company policies should be followed in any case. CSO should ensure that handing/taking over should be conducted timely. Although it is too late but CSO should complete all necessary documentation to avoid any inconvenience in future or any dispute. As per SOM, Clause, F-1. HANDING / TAKING OVER; a) “Whenever a BH, Accountant or Librarian transfers/Leaves the Company, he/she will have to hand over the charge to either his/her replacement or the person(s) nominated by the respective SGO/RO (CSO).” b) “Handing/taking over of the BH, Accountant or Librarian will be carried out under the supervision of the RO/CSO (normally Accounts Department/Regional (Cluster) Librarian). However, a representative from the Systems and Audit department will also participate in this process (other than librarian) as an observer.” For clarity of payables/receivables recorded in books of account, the balance confirmation certificates should be obtained.
observations.audit_view: The balance confirmation certificates were not provided till issuance of the report. However, during initial working (by the branch) unrecorded payable of Rs. 770,098 were claimed by different vendors. Though, the branch had agreed to pay Rs. 337,163 against such claims. It is recommended that such payables should be verified by the CSOC before further decisions. Snapshot of the table (shared by the branch is attached as under);

observations.title: Rate List of Livery Items not Available with Branch
observations.observation: Copy of Rate List for the purchase of current year’s Livery Items should be available in branch. It was observed that mentioned Rate List was not available with the branch.
observations.recommendation: Rate list of livery Items should be available with the branch for comparison of the variance. As per School Operations Manual, Clause, C-9.3 PURCHASE OF LIVERY ITEMS, b); “Manager Procurement and Asset Management will circulate a rate list of “livery items”, for Regions (Clusters) and Head Office yearly, stating against each the maximum amount that can be spent for procurement. These rate lists will preferably be circulated in the month of February.”
observations.audit_view: Branch did not provide/show such rate list to us till foolw up audit visit.

observations.title: Documents not Serial Numbered
observations.observation: As per policy, the official documents e.g. GRN, AIDN and Transfer Notes etc. should be serial numbered. During the audit it was observed that no such practice was in place.
observations.recommendation: Serial numbers should be assigned for identification of a document. As per SOM, Clause; G-1.9.5 ISSUANCE OF PURCHASE ORDER (PO), f) “The PR number shall be mentioned on …….. (The snap shot of PR is also attached for visual reference) E-1.4.2 GOODS RECEIVED NOTE (GRN), g) “All GRNs shall be sequentially numbered. Branch/Office shall assign numbers to manual GRNs starting with Branch/Office code: Br.Code - Sr.Number (e.g. for Garden town Branch 211-0001). New serial shall be used for each financial year.” E-1.7.3 ASSETS INSPECTION AND DISPOSAL NOTE (AIDN), e) “AIDNs shall be serially numbered” E-1.6.3 TRANSFER NOTE AND RELATED PROVISIONS, b) “Transfer notes shall be serially numbered. Each Office/Branch shall assign numbers to transfer notes starting with the Office/Branch code. New serial shall be started at the beginning of every financial year.”

observations.title: Excess Payment to PESSI
observations.observation: The payments should be released after due diligence. Whereas, it was observed that the payment to PESSI was made in excess. As per the branch record, the payment against PESSI was being made for the left employees. It was identified that Rs.70,350/- were paid in excess. Detail of few of such instances is as under; S.No Branch

observations.title: Delay in Providing Medical Insurance Cards to Employees
observations.observation: Medical Insurance Cards should be timely issued to employees, to avail medical insurance facility provided by the company. During scrutiny of employee record, it was observed that medical insurance cards for the year 2020 were not delivered to employees of the branch till September 2020, i.e. even after lapse of more than eight months.
observations.recommendation: To avoid difficulties in hospitalization procedure, cluster support office should ensure that medical insurance cards are provided on timely basis to all the employees. As per BEAMS, Handout for Medical Insurance Plan, How You Can Avail Treatment; “….. you are required to submit a copy of your health card”

observations.title: Recruitment & Selection Processing Record not Being Maintained
observations.observation: Record for decisions pertaining to recruitment and selection process should be maintained by the branch, for every post. During the audit, it was observed that the record was not being maintained.
observations.recommendation: Relevant record should be maintained for future reference. As per SOM, Clause, C-7.14 (a); “All decisions must be documented at each stage. Sufficient records must be kept explaining how the lists were compiled.”

observations.title: Discrepancies in Issuance of Appointment Letters & Joining of Employees
observations.observation: Employees should be issued appointment letters after finalizing terms and conditions pertaining to services. However, the appointment letters were being issued once employees were on board. Back dates for joining of the resources were mentioned on the appointment letters. Some of the instances are as under; 1st Attendance (b-a) Noureen Anjum Naila Javed Irfan Aslam Kiran Nadeem Rida Batool Arooj Fatima Sumera Mukhtar Ammara Hanif Sadia Waheed Syeda Hira Gulzar Asghar Khalid Lubna Jamil Abdul Rauf Muhammad Rashid Kaneez Niazi Resultantly (as per the detail provided by branch accountant) the employees’ joining and first attendance, was before the issuance of appointment letters. 1st Attendance (b-a) Noureen Anjum Naila Javed Irfan Aslam Kiran Nadeem Rida Batool Arooj Fatima Sumera Mukhtar Ammara Hanif Sadia Waheed Syeda Hira Gulzar Asghar Khalid Lubna Jamil Abdul Rauf Muhammad Rashid Kaneez Niazi
observations.recommendation: Appointment letters should be issued before employee joining. Remuneration and other working requirements (as the case may be) should be finalized before employee joining. As per SOM, C-7.11 APPOINTMENT LETTERS, f); “The appointment shall become effective from the date of joining as specified in the Appointment Letter and will be governed by the terms and conditions set out therein.”

observations.title: Detail of Next of Kin not Provided
observations.observation: As per company practice whenever an employee is hired he/she needs to provide information regarding “Next of Kin” in personal information form. Such information is helpful in case an employee suffers from any accident at work or any similar sort of issue. However, in some cases next of kin information was not provided in personal information form. Few of the instances are as under; Rabia Khan Syed Muhammad Talha Aiza Zahoor Shagufta Irshad Hamna Khakwani Nida Ahmad hashmi Riffat Chaudhry Hama81d Ejaz Noureen Anjum Saira Asif Abdul Rauf Arooj Fatima Irfan Aslam
observations.recommendation: As per SOM, Form # HRM010-B, such information is to be provided in Personal Information Form. Concerned branch personnel should review employee files and ensure that relevant information is being obtained as required.

observations.title: Registration Receipts not Signed by Parents / PRO
observations.observation: As per standard practice registration receipts should be signed by parents, and PRO. It was observed that the receipts were not being signed by parents and the PRO. The signatures were also found missing on copy of registration receipts submitted in accounts office.
observations.recommendation: Relevant personnel should ensure to obtain parents’ signature on registration receipts to get authentication of particulars; such as the Name, DOB, and Amount Received etc. PRO should also sign the receipts for future reference. Branch should send the files of Transferred-out students to the respective branch along with the Transfer Letter. According to the SOM, Clause, A-8 (d); “In case of transfer of a student, it shall be the responsibility of the PRO to promptly send the student file to the Concerned Branch after entering information in student module.”

observations.title: Unapproved Fee Concessions
observations.observation: Fee concession documents/approvals must be filed in student files so that these can be referred to at the time of need. While scrutinizing the student files it was observed that the approvals of fee concessions being availed by the students were not available. It was informed by the branch staff that none of the approvals for current and previous session have been received from CSO.
observations.recommendation: CSO should forward the approvals for all students to the branch for their record and reference and the same must be filed in student files.

observations.title: Student Security Refund Intimation not Sent
observations.observation: Information regarding security refund should be intimated to parents. It was observed that the policy prescribed for the purpose was not being complied. Branch was not sending the security refund intimation to parents.
observations.recommendation: Parents should be informed about security refund. As per SOM, Clause, A-4.3.3. SECURITY REFUND PROCEDURE; f)“If the entire student security has been adjusted, thus rendering the payable student security nil, then the student security refund form/fee exemption form stating the calculation shall be dispatched to the applicant for their information and to avoid unnecessary confusion; g) “The courier receipts are attached in support of the fee exemption/concession form or the security refund form, as the case may be.”

observations.title: Same Codes Affixed to Two Fixed Assets
observations.observation: Unique asset code should be affixed to each fixed asset. During physical checking of fixed assets, following assets were found having same asset codes. Detail is as under: Sr#

observations.title: Surplus/Not in use Assets Found in Branch
observations.observation: Surplus/unusable assets should be reported to CSO through AIDN so that they can be transferred to other branches where needed or disposed-off if necessary. During audit some surplus/unused assets were observed in branch. Detail is mentioned below:

observations.title: Discrepancies in FA Register Columns
observations.observation: As per company practice, complete information should be mentioned in fixed asset register. However, it was observed that certain columns were left blank e.g. GRN Receipt Number was not mentioned. Supplier Name was not mentioned. Invoice Number was not mentioned. PO Reference was not mentioned. Furthermore, Aspect of assets (Brand, Make, Model) should also be mentioned in fixed asset register. It was observed during physical verification and scrutiny of Fixed Asset Record, that, only category of assets were mentioned, but, aspects containing description of the assets were not available in fixed asset register of the branch.
observations.recommendation: Complete information should be mentioned in the FA Register.

observations.title: Aspects of Assets not Mentioned in Fixed Asset Register
observations.observation: Aspect of assets (Brand, Make, Model) should be mentioned in fixed asset register. It was observed during physical verification and scrutiny of Fixed Asset Record, that, only category of assets were mentioned, but, aspects containing description of the assets were not available in fixed asset register of the branch.
observations.recommendation: In order to physically verify the assets authentically with Brand, Make, Model and any other aspect with Fixed Asset Register of the branch, it is necessary to have the same information in FA register.

observations.title: Minutes of Librarian Meeting file not Available
observations.observation: Minutes of the librarian meeting with regional librarian should befiled by branch librarian. During the audit it was observed that branch had notminutes of the librarian meeting in their file.
observations.recommendation: Librarian should maintain the minutes file for reference as per Library Manual: “The Regional Librarian should call a meeting once/twice in a academic year of school librarians. All librarians are given minutes of that meeting. The librarian should file these.”

observations.title: Stock Taking not Done (2020)
observations.observation: As per the company policy physical stock taking of library books should be done at least once a year. However, in the branch such stock taking was not done after summer 2019.
observations.recommendation: Stock taking should be done as prescribed by policy. As per library manualclause 17.2; “Stocktaking …………………. at least once a year” Necessary steps should be taken for repair/ disposal of books. As per Library Manual, Clause 8.1; “To maintain the efficient running of the school library, constant maintaining of resources should be an ongoing procedure. The wear and tear of circulation requires that books should be mended, repaired, bound and re-bound so that they are maintained in a fit condition to be handled”.

observations.title: Incomplete/Wrong Data Entry in Library Module
observations.observation: Complete and correct information/ particulars should be entered in the library module. However, certain discrepancies were observed in this regard. Following is the detail; Books were entered in the module with zero price. Cost was missing against several books. Books with <200 cost were accessed in main register. Item call numbers were not mentioned. ISBN numbers were not mentioned. Author name not mentioned. Page numbers were not mentioned. Publisher name was missing. Publisher place was not mentioned. Copyright date was not mentioned. Copyright date was not mentioned. 0s1s13
observations.recommendation: Complete information i.e. Cost, Publisher Name, Item Call Number, ISBN, Author Name etc be enter. Should be entered. Correct cost should be mentioned. < 200 Books should not be accessed in Main Accession register.

observations.title: Non-compliance with Security Contract by Security Company
observations.observation: The armed guards at the branch are provided by Freedom Security Services. As per the contract, the security company has to provide 50% ex-armed forces personnel. It was informed by the branch security supervisor that only one out of seven armed guards provided by the security services provider were ex-armed forces personnel.
observations.recommendation: It is therefore recommended that the non-compliance of security services contract for providing 50% ex-army armed guards be reported to CSO and followed up on until issues are resolved. Additionally the security company should be penalized accordingly.

observations.title: No Backup system at Night in Case of Power Failure
observations.observation: Branch should have a backup system to keep the boundary lights on at night in case of Power failure. During audit it was observed that there was no lighting system in case of power failure (load shedding) at night. This could lead to some serious consequences given the current security conditions prevailing in the Country.
observations.recommendation: Some of the lights should be on UPS to avoid getting completely dark at night in load shedding durations.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Maintaining Science Lab Items & Registers
observations.observation: Science laboratory items and registers and should be maintained properly. During the audit certain discrepancies were found in this regard. Such as; Registers not checked as per the specified intervals. Certain items were obsolete/out of order/expired but not discarded. Several laboratory items which were never used for the last 7 years.
observations.recommendation: As per SOM, Clause; E-2.2 SCIENCE/GENERAL LABORATORY REGISTERS, f); “The BH shall verify the laboratory registers on a monthly basis.” Expired items should be disposed after due approval.

observations.title: Savings in Student Expenditure
observations.observation: As per Company policy, savings under the category of student expenses should be avoided. During review of “Budget Variance Sheets”, it was observed that budget for student expenditure remained un-utilized in certain heads of student expenses, for the year 2019-20, 2020-21, 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24. The detail is attached as Annexure-B.
observations.recommendation: Budget for student expenses should be fully utilized and savings in these heads of account should be avoided. As per School Operations Manual: “There should be no saving of funds under the category of ‘student expenses”.
observations.audit_view: The “COVID-19” factor had considerably reduced during the year 2021-22 however considerable under spending was observed. Hence the importance of consuming funds under ‘Student Expenditures’ is re-emphasized.

observations.title: Delayed Reimbursement of Claims by RO
observations.observation: Branch is being allocated limited budget against each head of account, late reimbursements to the Branch may lead to shortage of funds for smooth execution of operations. During current audit, some instances were observed where reimbursements were finalized/disbursed with significant delays to the Branch by ROC as applicable. For detail, please refer to Annexure-C.
observations.recommendation: To avoid unnecessary delays and shortage of funds in branch, reimbursement claims should be processed on timely basis by ROC. As per Policy: “All reimbursement claims received shall be checked by respective Accounts department within 20 days of their receipt”.
observations.audit_view: The purpose of stipulating a time period for reimbursements is to ensure smooth Branch operations. Therefore, compliance with company policy is re-emphasized.

observations.title: Departure Attendance not marked
observations.observation: Attendance should be marked while joining office at the start of day and leaving at day end. During audit, it was observed that some of the employees were not marking departure attendance on regular basis. A few of the instances are mentioned in Annexure E.
observations.recommendation: Branch Head should monitor the attendance record of the branch employees and ensure that the in case of any discrepancy in attendance, staff raise their application for “Attendance Not Marked”, or “Early Leaving” (whichever is applicable) highlighting the reasons. As per policy: “…. Employees shall mark their attendance on biometric devices (online attendance) installed in offices. Further; “Employees are advised to check their attendance on the BEAMS Online Attendance Module regularly to get any errors rectified (e.g. attendance not marked).”

observations.title: Out of Order Assets Found in Branch
observations.observation: All assets should be kept with due care; any damaged asset should be repaired or disposed-off. During physical verification many assets were found for which repair work/disposal was not initiated by the branch. Detail is attached in Annexure-G.
observations.recommendation: Branch management should take initiative to repair the highlighted assets. In case if they are beyond repair, these should be reported to ROC through AIDN so that they can be disposed-off. As per policy: “Where a Branch/RO has surplus assets for any reason, the same shall be communicated to the Manager P&AM at the ROC (RO) ……” Further: “Assets are sold when: ∙ Assets are beyond repair or where the cost of repair is considerably high and it is considered appropriate to buy a new asset ∙ Assets are obsolete ∙ The Company, for any other reason, has no use for the assets”

observations.title: Unnumbered Assets
observations.observation: All the Fixed Assets should be numbered with the Codes assigned to them. During physical verification of assets, on sample basis, some un-numbered assets were observed in the Branch. Detail of instances are mentioned in Annexure-H.
observations.recommendation: All the Fixed Assets should be numbered as per Fixed Asset Register. As per Policy: “Upon receipt of codes, Designated Officer of User Office shall affix these codes on respective fixed assets immediately. Such codes shall be affixed in a systematic and permanent manner”.

observations.title: Splitting of Transactions to Avoid CSQ Requirement
observations.observation: According to Company policy quotations should be obtained from 3 to 5 vendors for transactions exceeding PKR 25,000. During audit, certain cases were identified where this requirement was deliberately circumvented by splitting the activity into three transactions. During discussion Branch Officer Facility Administration (Mr. Adeel Malik) acknowledged the mistakes & lapses in compliance of company policy. There is a risk that task may have been assigned at higher rates to favourite vendors resulting in Financial Loss to the Company, further in absence of fair competition among vendor’s value for money cannot be achieved. Detail is as under: Activity Rewinding of Swimming pool exhaust fan Shalimar Electronics Rewinding of Swimming pool exhaust fan Shalimar Electronics Rewinding of Swimming pool exhaust fan Shalimar Electronics Neon Signs for Swimming pool Tufail Sons Neon Signs for Swimming pool Tufail Sons Neon Signs for Swimming pool Tufail Sons
observations.recommendation: Procurement procedure should be followed as mentioned in the policies. According to Policy: “Appropriate approval is mandatory to ascertain the sanctity of any transaction. Breaking or splitting a transaction into smaller values just to avoid approval from the concerned authorities will be considered as violation of this policy.” "A minimum of three vendors shall be included in the CSQ. In cases with fewer than three vendors, an exception must be granted in accordance with the 'Exception to Quotation' section." Branch Head and concerned staff are requested to ensure the compliance with company polices at the time of approval / review of transactions. List of Preferred Vendors should be available in the branch. As per policy: “For day to day procurement activities, vendors may not be formally registered, but a list of  preferred vendors shall be maintained. Officers responsible for procurement shall prepare a list of  suitable vendors/contractors. This list shall be reviewed/updated by members of the Purchase  Committee. The designated Officer will be responsible for maintaining and updating the list.”

observations.title: Fair Market Analysis not Performed for Branch Procurements
observations.observation: Procuring of services or goods worth more than Rs.25,000 should be followed by a CSQ, listing quotations from at least 3 vendors. During the analysis of imprests, it was observed that many items and services were availed without Fair Market analysis & CSQ. Detail of such activities is as following: Agha Transport JV-13 Coaster for students sports acticity ARZ Photography JV-15 Photography & video graphy for Graduation ceremoney ARZ Photography JV-15 Photography only for dream team activity Plan IT Events JV-9 Setup for annual play ARZ Photography JV-14 Photography For annual play ARZ Photography JV-7 Photography For Students activities Kreative Kreation JV-1 Fixing of vinyle sheets Plan IT Events JV-9 Setup for annual play Imran Sound System JV-9 Repairing of sound system of auditorium Kreative Kreation JV-31 Vinyle flexes with design and printing Recommendations: CSQ should contain three quotations from vendors unless stated exempted. As per policy: “Minimum three vendors shall be included in CSQ. In case of less than three vendors, exception shall be granted in accordance with Exception to Quotation section”

observations.title: Track Record of Quotation not Maintained by Branch
observations.observation: For procurements valuing more than Rs. 100,000, a track of quotations should be filed separately and made available for verification. It was observed during the audit that track records of such procurements were not kept by the branch.
observations.recommendation: The concerned staff at Branch should follow the procedure laid down in policy. According to policy: “For Procurements valuing more than Rs. 100,000 a track of quotations received shall be maintained at Branch duly authenticated by PC to ensure that all quotations received are properly accounted for.” To ensure transparency and accuracy of the activities conducted, it is recommended to record all the receipts and expenses of the activities conducted in a branch.
observations.audit_view: It was observed during a subsequent Audit Visit that inspite of updation from the branch, “Finanace Details” were still not appearing in the BEAMS.

observations.title: No Policy for Cambridge Refund Available in Branch
observations.observation: Students who do not appear for their exams but have submitted their registration fee are entitled to a refund, provided they inform the concerned person in a timely manner. There are also certain conditions under which the branch can withhold the refund. During the audit, it was observed that no clear policy existed for handling student refunds, leading to a credit balance accumulating in the ledger over the years, however, an e-mail was shouted by ROC for such guidelines.
observations.recommendation: To prevent ambiguity and maintain accurate financial records, a clear and comprehensive refund policy should be developed and made available at the branch. This policy should outline the eligibility criteria, timelines, and conditions under which refunds can be processed or withheld.

observations.title: Descrepancies in Bank Ledger Account
observations.observation: Payments made through bank account should contain a cheque # for reference. During audit it was observed that few bank payments did not have a cheque Number. Some of the instances are as below:

observations.title: Credit Balance of Cash in Hand Ledger
observations.observation: As per company policy, the balance of Cash in Hand Ledger should not be negative. During audit it was observed that closing balance of the ledger account was credit on many occasions. Instances are mentioned in below table: BALANCE

observations.title: Reason for Registration Fee Waiver not Mentioned
observations.observation: Student Registration data should be complete in all respect. It was observed during the audit that the reason for Free Registration was not mentioned in the BEAMS Registration Register. Instances are mentioned as Annexure-L.
observations.recommendation: Reason for the waiver in Registration fee should be mentioned in the BEAMS.

observations.title: Inventory Record of Land Lord’s Assets not Available
observations.observation: To avoid any confusion at the time of change in the building a list of fixed assets belonging to the building owner, kept in the branch’s premises, should be present in the branch. It was observed that the said list was not available with the branch.
observations.recommendation: The said list should be available with the branch to distinguish between company’s assets and the landlord’s assets. RO should provide the said list to branch.

observations.title: File of Clearance Forms not Maintained
observations.observation: File of Clearance Forms should be maintained by the branch. During audit it was observed that file Clearance Forms of Withdrawn Students and Left Employees was not prepared by the branch.
observations.recommendation: File should be prepare and updated on timely according to the Library Manual : “If a person lefts the system with outstanding books/library items, it should be mentioned on clearance form and keep record properly”.

observations.title: File for Reminders not Maintained
observations.observation: Reminders should be issued to the person who fail to submit the issued books on time to library. A file should be kept as a record for the reminders issued. It was observed that no file for reminders was maintained in library. Recommendations Reminders should be issued for the books that are over due and a file should be maintained for record. As per policy: “A file should be maintained with a copy of the Reminders issued to the teachers/students for not returning the books on time”
observations.recommendation: Keeping in view the importance of above mentioned features which are already available in existing open source library module (KOHA), there is a need to ensure to access and practice of these options for the more controlled, efficient, accurate and scrutinized working of branch librarians by utilizing the available resources.

observations.title: Emergency exits and Assembly area Unmarked
observations.observation: Emergency exits and Assembly areas should be clearly marked ensuring smooth evacuation of buildings. It was observed that no “exits” or “assembly area” were labelled in branch. There were also very few arrows directing towards exits on wall.
observations.recommendation: Emergency exits and assembly area should be clearly labelled as per the emergency plan of branch in order to ensure smooth evacuation.

observations.title: Insufficient Backup time of CCTV Cameras
observations.observation: Sufficient back up time of CCTV Cameras should be available for better security controls. It was observed during current audit that there was 10 days backup time of one DVRs having 16 CCTV cameras.
observations.recommendation: At least 15 days backup time should be maintained for security purposes. As per Security Guidelines of BSS Pakistan, Clause 3D “Keep CCTV Recording/Tape for 15 days at least.”

observations.title: Evacuation Plans not Displayed
observations.observation: Evacuation plans should be displayed on every floors of the building to provide ensure effective evacuation through out the building in case of emergencies. During Audit it was noticed that no such plan was displayed in the building.
observations.recommendation: Evacuation plans should be displayed on every floors at visible locations.

observations.title: Incomplete Generator Log Book
observations.observation: Generator Log book should be prepared, maintained and signed by the generator  operator and caretaker. During audit, it was found that the Log Book was not maintained as per directives. Following objections were observed: Missing entries for fuel refilled in generator. No details of maintenance activities. No meter Reading mentioned. No fuel average calculated.
observations.recommendation: Generator Log book record should be updated monthly by Branch OFA and Branch Head. As per policy “Officer Facility Administration (OFA) / Administration Officer (AO) shall maintain the record (logbook & invoices) pertinent to generator operations including fueling for their respective Branches / Offices. Following information shall be recorded in the logbook on daily basis: Date & time of diesel re-filling Quantity of fuel filled Meter readings before and after the fueling Running hours of generator and time Fuel average Replacement of parts, if any Detail of other maintenance activities e.g. change of engine oil, fuel filter, air filter etc.”

observations.title: Fake Quotations
observations.observation: There were 03 cases amounting to Rs. 101,293 in which procurement process was not followed. Apparently, fake quotations were prepared/obtained just to fulfil documentation/filing requirements and not for fair price competition It shows that Officials involved in procurement did not exercise due care while discharging their duties/responsibilities. The detail is attached as Annexure-I.
observations.recommendation: Company policies and controls over the purchase/procurement procedures should be applied and exercised by the school management in true spirit. Purchase committee need to perform active role in the purchase process. Loose controls may result in financial losses to the organization. Branch Head shall ensure that procurement was made in accordance with Company’s policies i.e. Quotations have been obtained. Comparative Statements have been prepared. Purchase/Work order have been issued and duly accepted by vendors. In case a valid reason for not following stipulated procedure exists it should be properly documented and duly approved/signed by the competent authority. As per SOM, Clause; G-1.9.2 QUOTATIONS, g); “For procurement valuing more than PKR 100,000, a track of quotations received shall be maintained at the Branch, duly authenticated by the PC to ensure that all quotations received are properly accounted for.” According to SOM, Clause, G-1.9.2 (a); “A Request for Quotation (RFQ) shall be used for the procurement of items having a cost/value of more than PKR 25,000 per item/transaction. “ According to SOM, Clause, G-1.9.4 (c); “c)The PC shall prepare a “Comparative Statement of Quotations”. Preferably three to five vendors shall be included in the Statement.” According to SOM, Clause, G-1.9.2 (h); “h)In certain cases, supplier selection can be made at the beginning of a financial year for that financial year. The most favourable supplier, quality wise, cost wise etc., should be selected. In cases such as  where the supplier has not increased his price, altered quality from his previous supply or prices on the whole have not decreased in the market, a fresh quotation will not be obtained. However, a review will be carried out 6 months after the first quotations were obtained, by obtaining fresh quotations to ensure the most favourable terms. “ As per SOM, Clause, G-1.9.5 (b); PO is mandatory for procurement of item having cost/value of Rs. 25,000 or above. “The PO shall not be mandatory for procurement of items having a cost/value of less than PKR 25,000/-“

observations.title: Discrepancies in Vendor Management
observations.observation: During the audit certain discrepancies were observed in vendor management. Vendors Registration not in Practice Record of all vendors engaged in business with the branch should be filed separately and made available for verification. Whereas, it was observed that record of “Registered Vendors”, such as Vendors Registration Application Forms (VRA) and supporting documents were not available for any vendors. Approved Vendors List not Available with Branch Branch should have approved list of preferred vendors for its daily and/or routine procurement (where vendors may not be formally registered). It was observed that such list was not prepared by purchase committee.
observations.recommendation: The concerned staff at CSO/Branch should follow the procedure laid down for vendor registration in SOM. As per SOM, Clause, G-1.6 (f); “The files of applicants/vendors shall also be maintained by the designated Officer of the Branch and be available for review by Head of P&AM and authorised P&AM staff.” As per the SOM, Clause H1.6.f), d) & e): “The person nominated from the Branch side in the SGO(CSO)CC shall coordinate for collection of required data to be examined and included in the contractor/vendor database/list (for successful cases). The SGO(CSO)CC, after its satisfaction, shall approve the contractor/vendor for inclusion in the contractor/vendor database/list. The said database/list shall be maintained at the concerned SGO(CSO) by the SGO(CSO)CC”. “The standard for registration of contractors/vendors that provide services/goods with a value less than PKR 100,000 per annum shall require a less stringent level of verification than the minimum standards set above. In these cases, upon registration, the contractor/vendor file must indicate that the contractor/vendor is registered to do business with the Company, but on a minor scale and only for contracts below PKR 100,000 per annum.” As per Procurement Manual, Clause; 6.2.3;“Vendor shall submit the completed vendor registration application along with required documents (if any) to respective procurement department or accounts office (in-case of branches) which shall be forwarded promptly to the branch PC”. 6.8.6; “The files of applicants / vendors shall also be maintained by the designated officer of P&AM department / PC (in-case of branches) and be available for review by Head of P&AM and authorized P&AM staff.” As per SOM, Clause, G-1.6(d); “For day to day procurement activities, vendors may not be formally registered, but a list shall be maintained for preferred vendors. Officer responsible for procurement shall prepare list of suitable vendors/contractors. This list shall be reviewed/updated by the members of Purchase Committee”.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Applications for “Outstation”

observations.recommendation: The leaves should be approved with due care. “Outstation” should be applied for the official visits or meeting at the place other than premises where an employee works. For compensation of working on off days, an application for toil should be raised prescribing necessary information. As per SOM, Clause, C-4.5.7 COMPENSATORY LEAVE (TOIL), b); “An employee who is required to perform official duty after office hours on an off day and/or gazetted holiday, shall be entitled to Compensatory Leave provided prior approval of the relevant authority was obtained………….”

observations.title: Delay in Payment of Fuel Allowance
observations.observation: Fuel allowance should be paid in accordance to the timeline defined by the company policy. While scrutinizing, branch records we identified that there were instances in which delays were observed in payment of Fuel of Allowance by CSO. Detail of the few of the delays is attached in Annexure-R.
observations.recommendation: Fuel allowance should be paid in accordance to time period specified in SOM. As per SOM, Clause; D-2.6 (c):“After receiving the original fuel slips, the Branch Accountant shall prepare the fuel allowance claims of entitled employees along with the summary and forward it to the RO(CSO).” D-2.6 (d);“The RO(CSO) shall send cheques for fuel allowances from the 10th to the 15th of every month.”

observations.title: Registration Cash Short Deposited
observations.observation: Deposit of Registration amount on weekly basis or immediately when it reaches to Rs. 10,000 is directed in the manual. However, while scrutinizing the registration receipts record we found that an amount of Rs. 26,400 was short deposited in company account by the concerned staff of branch on account of registration fee. Detail is mentioned as below:

observations.title: Discrepancies in Collection of Registration Fee & Receipts
observations.observation: During the audit certain discrepancies were found in collection and deposit of registration fee. Such as, “Registration Receipt Number” was not appearing in “Registration List”, and ID # issued in the “Registration List” was not appearing on “Registration Receipt”. This anomaly was causing a break in link of both the reports, and hence completeness of registration fee deposit could not be verified. Emails/ Circulars for Registration rates were not available/filed with PRO/Accountant. Since the rate is fed manually the PRO should maintain a record for future purposes. This acted as a hinderance in ensuring compliance of prescribed rates. Bank deposit slips and registration receipts were not validated by branch head.
observations.recommendation: Numbering should be done to create a link in both reports. Complete record should be maintained. Relevant emails, circulars for waivers, and discounts should be filed for future reference. Branch Head should intensify the monitoring mechanism to ensure that all the receipts are deposited on timely basis. As per SOM, Clause,  A-1.6 BANK DEPOSIT OF REGISTRATION FEE, a); “Cash collected as Registration Fee shall be deposited in the bank by close of every working week……..”. Relevant circular (for 50% registration fee) should be retrieved for future reference.

observations.title: Incomplete Parents’ Information for Students in BEAMS

During scrutiny of students’ record in BEAMS we found that parents’ information data of few students was not completely updated in BEAMS. Details of such instances, extracted from BEAMS have been given in Annexure-T.
observations.recommendation: Complete information should be updated in BEAMS on an early basis.

observations.title: No Record for Sending Files of Transfer Out Students
observations.observation: Dispatch record along with receiving of files forwarded for students transferred-out to other branches should be available with the transferring branch. The branch could not provide evidence of dispatching the files and/or recipient acknowledgement. This reveals that such record was not being maintained.
observations.recommendation: Branch should maintain record of dispatch and obtain acknowledgement from relevant recipients.

observations.title: Un Disclosed Sale Proceeds of Fixed Assets
observations.observation: During the branch audit of Bosan Road Campus, Multan an AIDN was checked. In the course of such proceedings it was observed that amount deposited in company’s bank account was not tallied with the actual sale proceeds. The initial declared sale proceeds was of Rs. 133,610 whereas the deposit slip attached against this sale proceed was of Rs. 99,290 only. Upon inquiry, another deposit slip amounting to Rs. 34,320 was shared (for scrap items) by accounts staff and they also informed that total sale proceeds were amounting to Rs. 145,000 instead of Rs. 133,610 (creating a difference of Rs 11,390) and this additional amount (sale proceed) is withheld with them. According to Branch Accountants, this un-deposited amount (Rs. 11,390) was generated against sale of assets which were written-off in previous year(s) and now when traced, these were sold without any disclosure and approval from competent authority. Refer; Annexure-U (Detail of Sale Proceeds) Annexure-V (Scanned images of Deposit Slips). Annexure-W (For scanned image of the deposit slip against assets sold without disclosure). Annexure-X (List of assets sold without disclosure). Annexure-Y (Cash Receipt evidence provided by vendor). Further Discrepancies Certain other anomalies were also observed out of which few of the significant issues are being shared; According to the SOM, the amount against sale proceeds should be collected before handing over assets to successful bidder, and the amount should actually be deposited in main bank account. Whereas, according to the Gate Record, the assets were taken away from the branch during 12-Sep-2020 to 17-Sep-2020 and the amount was deposited after two three days (i.e. on 15-Sep-2020 and 19-Sep-2020). As per the company policy, Gate Pass should be prepared before moving the assets out of branch. Whereas, the relevant Security Supervisor (Mr. Afzal Nadeem) informed that the gate pass was prepared after the transaction, when the assets were actually taken away from the branch.
observations.recommendation: Such practices should be avoided. Fixed Asset Section (Fin Ops) is requested to look into the matter.
observations.audit_view: The matter has been taken up by Fixed Asset Section (Fin Ops) and Fixed Asset Verification activity has been initiated.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Daycare Facility at School
observations.observation: The daycare facility at school should be operated as prescribed by OPS Handbook 1. However, certain discrepancies were identified, few of which are; CCTV camera was out of order. Space for Infant & Children of other ages was not separated. Warning device for fire alarm was not available. Smoke detector was not installed. Fire extinguisher was not available.
observations.recommendation: As per OPS Handbook 1; A CCTV must be installed in the daycare. “Each space within a daycare facility that is used for the care of infants must be separate from spaces used by children of other ages. An early warning device shall be provided for sounding a fire alarm. An operable smoke detector must be placed in the daycare room. A fire extinguisher must also be in tact in the daycare facility.”

observations.title: Approved Copy of Handing/Taking over of Librarian (Primary Section) not Available
observations.observation: As per policy, approved copy for the Handing over/Taking over document of Librarian should be available in the branch. Mr. Nusrat Inbasat took over the charge of Branch Head from Ms. Sadia Islam in the Year 2015, but, the approved copy of Handing/Taking Over was not available with branch.
observations.recommendation: As per SOM, Clause F-1; a) “Whenever a …….. or Librarian transfers/Leaves the Company, he/she will have to hand over the charge to either his/her replacement or the person(s) nominated by the respective SGO/RO(CSO).” l) “A handing/taking over certificate will be duly signed by the Officials handing over charge and the Official taking over along with RO(CSO)-Accounts and S&A representatives.”

observations.recommendation: The Library space should be managed in accordance with the number of books present in the library. More racks may be added by branch in the library for proper display of books.

observations.title: Issues in Coverage of Security Camera
observations.observation: The installation and positioning of CCTV cameras should be in such a way that these are capable of covering all the building and its surroundings. During audit it was noted that CCTV cameras were not covering the whole premises as there were a number of blind spots around the main boundary wall. There was no surveillance inside the school premises. Moreover, 08 out of 28 cameras were out of order and 01 out of order (old) PTZ camera was found placed in the cabinet. Further, the positioning of few of the cameras were not focusing on the required areas.
observations.recommendation: Branch management should look into the matters and Blind spots should be removed by making adjustments in the camera positing as well as shifting of cameras. Surveillance inside the building should be enhanced. Positioning should be adjusted. Cameras should be repaired. Old PTZ Cameras should be repaired. If not repairable should be disposed off as per policy.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Precautionary Measures for Generator
observations.observation: As per standard practice the access to the generator is restricted through a fence or grill. However, no such safety measure was taken for 20 KVA Generator. Please refer to annexed snapshot for visual reference. Furthermore, open wires observed in the generator.
observations.recommendation: Remedial actions should be taken to restrict access to the generator. Grills should be properly affixed, and access should be secured. Open wires should be covered.

observations.title: Anomalies in Usage of 20 KVA Generator
observations.observation: The company assets should be properly used. The generator was provided to “Bosan Road Campus Multan” in July 2017 (transfer note not traced in branch records). According to branch personnel (verbal) the generator was installed to provide power backup to Admin Block. However, since then the generator was used only once (verbally informed by the branch personnel). During the visit of S&A, as well, the generator was not used. Instead of this the 150 KVA generator was being used for the power backup to admin block. Despite of the fact that the generator was not used in (almost) last three years, maintenance services were being done and the maintenance company was being paid for their visits.
observations.recommendation: Company assets should be used properly. The generator should be utilized according to the capacity. If the 20 KVA generator is sufficient for power back-up to Admin Block, 150 KVA generator should not be used. If a generator is not in use, same should be communicated to CSO so that; The generator is transferred to the branch, where it is required. Maintenance contract is adjusted accordingly.

observations.title: Record for Outward Gate Passes and Return of Items not Maintained Properly
observations.observation: To maintain an effective and complete track over outward movement of assets through the branch, record of outward gate passes and the track of return of these items (if to be returned) should be maintained. During the audit it was observed that such record was not being properly maintained.
observations.recommendation: In order to have better control over movement of goods, branch should properly maintain outward gate passes and the track record for return of these items (where appliable). The document tracking sheet should be attached to the documents being forwarded to different departments/offices. As per SOM, Clause, D-4 DOCUMENT TRACKING SHEET; “The “DOCUMENT TRACKING SHEET” attached as SOM001-N should be used on top of every document(s) that involves movement within different organisational tiers or departments. The main purpose of this sheet is to avoid/identify certain delays during various steps involved in completing document flows. Some important ones include: AIDNS for disposal of assets / scrap Cases of final settlement Reimbursement claims etc. It is also advisable to use this sheet in other relevant situations. Appropriate usage of this sheet can enhance workflow efficiency by highlighting various catch-points besides forcing slow movers to pick up their pace and move the chain of activities along.”

The items allocated should be properly used.

observations.recommendation: Contracts should be made for such services, and a copy should be maintained in branch files.

observations.title: Contracts with Third Parties not Filed/Placed in Branch
observations.observation: To ensure compliance to the terms and condition agreed between the ESL and vendors, a copy of contract should be available with the branch. During the audit, we found that agreement/contracts such as Security Guards, Generators Maintenance, UPS Maintenance, Maintenance of Walkthrough Gates Maintenance etc. we’re not available with the branch. In order to keep an eye on compliance by such companies the contract should have been available at branch level.
observations.recommendation: The contracts should be properly filed. Moreover, branch personnel should ensure that vendor are providing agreed level of services. Any issues must be highlighted within stipulated time so that remedial actions are taken in time.

Upon querying, the concerned accountant informed that; File for previous contract have been lost. Services for Year 2020 were acquired without a contract. observations.recommendation: File for previous contracts should be traced. Current year contract should be made after due rate verification.
